'''''Gypsophila vaccaria''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]]. It is native from [[Portugal]] and [[Morocco]] to the [[Himalayas]], and has been introduced into temperate areas worldwide.<ref name=POWO_154685-1/> Among its many [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]] is '''''Vaccaria hispanica''''', which was the only species placed in the genus '''''Vaccaria'''''. It is known by several common names including '''cowherb''', '''cowcockle''',<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242000971 Flora of North America]</ref> '''cow basil''',  '''cow soapwort''', and  '''prairie carnation'''. It is an annual herb with blue-gray, waxy herbage and pale pink flowers.

The [[seed]]s of the species are used in [[Traditional Chinese medicine|Chinese medicine]].<ref>''Chinese Herbal Medicine Materia Medica'', 3rd edition. Dan Bensky, Steven Clavey, Erich Stöger, et al. 2004. Eastland Press.</ref>
